title: Detection of inert cocartesian edges by target color projections
statement: Use the universes, coherent triangles and quasicategories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], monoidal infinity categories and inert maps of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], and cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ be a monoidal infinity category. Let $u:x\to y$ lie over an inert map $\alpha:[s]\to[r]$, where $s,r\geq0$. For each $1\leq i\leq r$, choose a $p$-cocartesian edge $t_i:y\to y_i$ over the consecutive-edge projection $\rho_i:[r]\to[1]$, and a coherent triangle with short edges $u,t_i$ and long edge $w_i:x\to y_i$ over $\rho_i\alpha$. Then $u$ is $p$-cocartesian if and only if every $w_i$ is $p$-cocartesian. This holds for every choice of the projections and triangles. For $r=0$ the condition is empty, so every edge over an inert map to $[0]$ is $p$-cocartesian. No cocartesianness of $u$ is assumed when choosing its target color projections, and no colimits are required.

source.place: Definition 3.1.13 and Definition 3.1.15; color-projection criterion used in Appendix A.3.4 and HA Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof invariant (ii), printed pp. 335–341. Generic monoidal form extracted from the returned Step 6; agent expansion via cocartesian mapping squares and the Segal equivalence. Read online 2026-10-17; shared archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: For the forward implication, suppose $u$ is $p$-cocartesian. In each given triangle the first short edge $u$ and the second short edge $t_i$ are cocartesian. The cancellation clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] therefore makes the long edge $w_i$ cocartesian. This includes the empty family when $r=0$.

For the converse choose a $p$-cocartesian lift $v:x\to x^{\prime}$ of $\alpha$; it exists because $p$ is a cocartesian fibration. Put $\mathcal F=\mathcal V^{\otimes}_{[r]}$. The lift $v$ is initial in the quasicategory $L(x,\alpha)$ of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. The given edge $u$ is another object of this category. Its mapping space from $v$ is contractible, hence nonempty, so a morphism gives an edge $e:x^{\prime}\to y$ in $\mathcal F$ and a coherent triangle $ev\simeq u$ over the triangle $(\alpha,1_{[r]},\alpha)$.

source.place: Remark 2.4.1.9, dual: initial cocartesian lifts and their comparison triangles.

proof.text: Choose coherent transport functors $T_i:\mathcal F\to\mathcal V^{\otimes}_{[1]}$ over $\rho_i$, with cocartesian transformations $a_i(c):c\to T_i(c)$. These are the transport functors of the Segal definition. Their coherent existence can be obtained from [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] by applying it to the inclusion $\mathcal F\to\mathcal V^{\otimes}$ and the constant transformation $\rho_i$ of its base diagram, in a containing universe in which this indexing simplicial set is small. The mapping-space criterion identifies that lemma's mapping-square notion of cocartesianness with the horn notion used here. The Segal axiom says $T=(T_i)_i:\mathcal F\to(\mathcal V^{\otimes}_{[1]})^r$ is a functor equivalence. For each $i$, both $a_i(y)$ and the prescribed $t_i$ are cocartesian lifts with source $y$ over $\rho_i$. Initiality of lifts gives a comparison equivalence $b_i:T_i(y)\to y_i$ in the fiber over $[1]$ with a coherent triangle $b_i a_i(y)\simeq t_i$.

source.place: Definition 2.2.6(1)-(2); coherent transport via HTT Proposition 3.1.2.1 and uniqueness via Remark 2.4.1.9, dual.

proof.text:
Assume all $w_i$ are cocartesian. Set $v_i=a_i(x^{\prime})v$ and $q_i=b_iT_i(e):T_i(x^{\prime})\to y_i$. Composition/cancellation makes $v_i$ cocartesian over $\rho_i\alpha$. Naturality of $a_i$ along $e$, followed by the comparison triangle for $b_i$ and by $ev\simeq u$, gives the coherent composite triangle
$$q_i v_i\simeq b_iT_i(e)a_i(x^{\prime})v\simeq b_i a_i(y)ev\simeq t_i u\simeq w_i.$$
The coherent transport transformations supply the square in this calculation; coherent composition and its associativity are those of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. All base triangles are the corresponding compositional triangles of the ordinary nerve, so this is a morphism in $L(x,\rho_i\alpha)$ from $v_i$ to $w_i$. Both its endpoints are initial cocartesian lifts. Their comparison is an equivalence in that lift category, and forgetting the triangle makes $q_i$ an equivalence in the fiber over $[1]$. Since $b_i$ is also an equivalence, $T_i(e)$ has invertible component class $[b_i]^{-1}[q_i]$, hence is an equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.1.7 and Remark 2.4.1.9, dual; agent expansion of the target-color comparison.

proof.text: The edge $T(e)$ is an equivalence in the product: take the inverses and both inverse triangles coordinatewise. Let $G$ be a quasi-inverse of the Segal equivalence $T$ and $\eta:1_{\mathcal F}\simeq GT$ its coherent natural equivalence. In $h\mathcal F$, naturality says $[e]=[\eta_y]^{-1}[G(T(e))][\eta_{x^{\prime}}]$. Each factor is invertible, so [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] identifies $e$ as an equivalence edge of $\mathcal F$. This argument uses the quasi-inverse in the definition of functor equivalence, rather than an uncited conservativity theorem.

source.place: Definition 2.2.6(2); explicit inverse argument for conservativity of the Segal equivalence.

proof.text: The fiber inclusion carries the inverse edge and inverse triangles of $e$ to the total quasicategory, so $e$ is an equivalence there too. By [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], precomposition with an inverse of $e$ is a homotopy inverse to precomposition with $e$ on every mapping space. In the square of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] for $e$, the bottom map is the identity, since $p(e)=1_{[r]}$, and the top map is this homotopy equivalence. The path-space pullback along the identity is equivalent to the upper-right mapping space by evaluation, with inverse the constant-path inclusion; thus this square is a homotopy pullback. The criterion makes $e$ cocartesian. Cancellation in the triangle with short edges $v,e$ now makes its long edge $u$ cocartesian. The original $t_i$ and triangles were arbitrary throughout, proving independence of choices.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3 and Proposition 2.4.1.7, dual; agent expansion for a vertical equivalence.

proof.text: For $r=0$, the Segal equivalence is $\mathcal F\simeq *$. Every edge in the one-point quasicategory is an equivalence, so the inverse argument of Step 5 makes the comparison $e$ in Step 2 an equivalence without any color tests. Step 6 then proves that $u$ is cocartesian. This works for every $s$: inert maps $[s]\to[0]$ are opposite to the inclusions of any one vertex $[0]\to[s]$, not just the identity at $[0]$. Thus the nullary clause of the original statement is valid and requires no added hypothesis.

source.place: Definitions 2.2.3 and 2.2.6(2), including the zeroth Segal product.

split_report.summary: Retained the original statement, including its nullary clause, and repaired the saved attempt: its proposed r>=1 restriction was unjustified and its mapping-space formula had the wrong variance. The seven-step proof factors through an initial cocartesian lift, identifies its transported comparison with comparisons between initial color lifts, detects its inverse through the Segal functor equivalence, and applies the mapping-space criterion and cancellation. No new nodes.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q33-581b775fa (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item, all 7 cited statements, both users (kan-filling Step 6, color-reconstruction Step 8) and the unit. It has no new nodes, and the statement is unchanged and true. The proof factors u as e∘v with v a cocartesian lift, which is initial in L(x,α). Each w_i ≃ (b_i T_i(e) a_i(x'))∘v, so two cancellations make w_i cocartesian exactly when T_i(e) is an equivalence. The Segal equivalence turns this into e being an equivalence, and cancellation in the triangle (v,e,u) then gives u cocartesian. I tested r=0 (fiber ≃ point, any vertex of [s]), r=1 with α the identity, s=0 and a non-invertible vertical e; all agree with the statement. Steps 1-7 use only what the cited statements say (cancellation/initiality, pointwise transport, mapping criterion, mapping composition), with the correct orientation and base triangles. Turning the class equality in Step 4 into a 2-simplex is glossed but routine. All cited statements are in the unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, so no tool_uses are needed and none are accepted, and there is no cycle (505-node traversal). It is not a duplicate: lem-coef-symmetric-inert-projection-detection works over Fin_* and lem-coef-inert-relative-tuple-cone is about limit cones. Minor provenance point: source.place still cites GH 3.1.13/3.1.15 while the steps cite 2.2.6/2.2.13; the source is not archived (WANTED, proof_origin agent), so I left it as is. No fixes; review.md written.

lean.statement: theorem operadic_inert_factor_equivalence {E : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory E] (p : E ⟶ monoidalSimplexBase.{u}) (_hp : IsMonoidalInfinityCategory p) {s r : ℕ} (α : op ⦋s⦌ ⟶ op ⦋r⦌) (_hα : IsMonoidalInert α) (u : Δ[1] ⟶ E) (_hu : u ≫ p = monoidalBaseEdge α) (t w : Fin r → (Δ[1] ⟶ E)) (σ : Fin r → (Δ[2] ⟶ E)) (_ht : ∀ i : Fin r, t i ≫ p = monoidalBaseEdge (monoidalRho i)) (_ht_cocartesian : ∀ i : Fin r, IsCocartesianEdge p (t i)) (_hσ₀₁ : ∀ i : Fin r, stdSimplex.δ 2 ≫ σ i = u) (_hσ₁₂ : ∀ i : Fin r, stdSimplex.δ 0 ≫ σ i = t i) (_hσ₀₂ : ∀ i : Fin r, stdSimplex.δ 1 ≫ σ i = w i) (_hσ_base : ∀ i : Fin r, σ i ≫ p = monoidalBaseTriangle α (monoidalRho i)) : IsCocartesianEdge p u ↔ ∀ i : Fin r, IsCocartesianEdge p (w i)
